question: Pooled across 22 contracts, does non-commercial positioning percentile predict 4-week forward returns (contrarian or momentum)?
metrics: IN beta +0.00047 t_clustered 0.16 R2 0.000 q-spread +0.107% | OOS beta -0.00296 t -0.56 R2 0.0001 q-spread +0.102%
robustness: instrument fixed effects, date-clustered SEs, non-overlapping 4w windows, 22 instruments, n=8049
decision: CLOSE the positioning-percentile hypothesis. H12 dead in both directions (contrarian and momentum). Do not re-run without a new information source (e.g. options/13F positioning, not COT percentile).
notes: The single-instrument sweep (59 tests) had no power; the panel does, and the effect is zero. This is a negative result with power, which is worth more than ten ambiguous ones.

question: Does an event (OPEX, FOMC, month-end, VIX first crossing 30) condition the payoff of a weak 5-day sign rule?
metrics: IS FOMC interaction beta +0.00204 t=2.23; OPEX t=-0.08; MONTH_END t=-0.23; VIX_ONSET30 t=-0.40
robustness: instrument fixed effects, date-clustered SEs, 22,799 IS rows / 10,546 OOS
result_status: FAIL (FOMC interaction significant in-sample but flips sign out-of-sample: -0.00113)

notes: FOMC day |SPY move| is only 1.09x a random day — the meeting matters less than the narrative.

question: Is the dealer-gamma exposure overlay anything more than volatility targeting in disguise?
metrics: gamma arm IS 0.767 / OOS 0.674; vol-target arm IS 0.700 / OOS 0.632; Δ(IS) +0.067 at 88.5th pct, Δ(OOS) +0.041 at 74.0th pct (bar 95)
robustness: circular-shift null on the Δ statistic, mean exposure matched, look-ahead-free vol scaling clipped [0,2]
decision: Close H17: the gamma overlay is volatility targeting with a gamma label. Use vol targeting (free, robust) for sizing; do not pay for gamma data to size a single-index book.
notes: Max drawdown did improve vs buy-and-hold (-27% vs -51% on the GEX sample) — a risk result, not an alpha result.

question: Does the CBOE volatility term structure forecast a volatility ONSET early enough to be worth acting on, beyond plain volatility targeting?
split: walk-forward, refit each January (no look-ahead) + 70/30 economic split
metrics: forward-8d onset AUC: VIX>30 onset 0.665, RV-expansion onset 0.746 (Brier skill +0.168); economic overlay IS 0.679 / OOS 0.555 vs vol-targeting 0.661 / 0.833; Δ(A−B) OOS −0.278 (pct 10.5)
robustness: 200 circular shifts of the weight series; mean exposure matched to the vol-targeting arm
decision: Term structure is a real variance forecaster (AUC 0.746) and belongs in the sizing/context layer and the daily brief. It is NOT an alpha signal: acting on it loses to free vol targeting by −0.28 Sharpe OOS.
notes: First version of this test printed Sharpe 1.98/2.28 because weights were applied same-bar and the label was coincident — see PITFALLS #15. Fixed before the verdict.

question: Does the Treasury curve slope (10y−3m, 10y−2y) pay for duration exposure via carry/roll-down?
robustness: terciles from trailing 3y (causal), circular-shift null, buy-and-hold AND vol-targeting arms both reported
decision: Curve slope does not pay duration exposure at the pre-declared bar. Documented side-effect: the rule halved the 2022-2026 bond drawdown (IEF maxDD −17.5% vs buy&hold's worse), i.e. it is risk avoidance, not alpha.
notes: OOS slice (2020-2026) is a single bond bear market — no regime breadth.

question: Do any of 5 classic hour-scale FX rules survive REAL quoted bid/ask spreads and one-bar execution latency?
cost_assumptions: one side of THAT BAR's measured quoted spread per unit of |delta position| (floor: no commission/slippage)
metrics: pooled net Sharpe IS/OOS: REV1 −7.83/−5.81, REV6 −3.02/−2.39, MOM12 −3.87/−2.49, BREAK −1.52/−0.44, HOURSEAS −10.83/−8.18; REV1 gross +0.188 bp/h vs net −0.154 bp/h (drag 0.342)
robustness: 200 circular shifts of each position series, 99th-percentile bar, all 5 signals reported
decision: Hourly FX direction is dead at retail cost. The one real finding: 1-hour reversal has a genuine GROSS edge (+0.19 bp/h) that is destroyed by always-on turnover.
notes: Cost wall is the whole story: at 1 trade/hour the spread is paid 24x a day.

question: Can sparse gating (big-move only, London/NY overlap only, both) rescue the hourly reversal that died on turnover?
robustness: 3 pre-declared variants, 98.33rd-percentile Bonferroni bar, OOS confirmation required
decision: Gating halves the loss and never flips the sign: quoted spreads would have to be 3-30x tighter than Dukascopy's to break even. That is an institutional-ECN number, not a retail one. Close H20 both directions.
notes: Breakeven multiple < 1 in every variant = the rule needs cheaper execution, not a better gate.

question: Do US congressional trade disclosures (House PTR) predict 21-day excess returns on a matched large-cap panel?
dataset_id: data/congress/congress_trades.csv (6,365 parsed PTR rows) + data/stocks (115 names)
cost_assumptions: 2 bp per side on a 21-day hold
metrics: IS: buys -0.69% vs sells -0.07% (diff -0.61pp), buys vs matched control 0.0th pct (control +0.61%). OOS: buys +2.60% vs sells -0.78% (diff +3.39pp), 99.5th pct (control +0.75%).
robustness: 200 matched-control draws per event (random dates, same ticker); returns are excess over the equal-weight panel to strip the market move
decision: No edge claim. The halves disagree in the strongest possible way (0th vs 99.5th percentile), which is exactly what a 16-month large-cap sample produces by chance. H21 stays OPEN pending a longer filing history, not closed.
notes: First test using non-price information. Example of why the pre-declared both-halves bar matters: a study that reported only the OOS window would have claimed a 99.5th-percentile edge.
